extra_misconceptions.fact: Gasoline vapors are heavier than air and settle in the lowest part of the bilge, requiring four minutes of blower operation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gasoline fumes rise quickly into the open air from an uncovered boat bilge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Exhaust gases pool near the swim platform and backdraft into open cockpits at slow speeds or when idling with a tailwind.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon monoxide only accumulates inside enclosed cabin cruisers and never on open runabouts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A propeller can still freewheel or engage accidentally in neutral, so the engine must be shut off before a swimmer nears the stern.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shifting an outboard motor into neutral stops the propeller from spinning in the water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Staying with a floating, capsized hull conserves body heat and gives rescuers a much larger visual target than a lone swimmer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Crew members should swim immediately for the nearest shoreline if their motorboat capsizes.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to gasoline vapors inside an enclosed bilge compartment before the blower runs?
Which physical indicator distinguishes early carbon monoxide poisoning from ordinary seasickness?
Under what condition does a slow-moving hull create the highest carbon monoxide concentration at the stern?
Why is it dangerous to leave the engine in gear while approaching a swimmer who fell overboard?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Type III vests are designed for conscious swimmers in calm inland water and require the wearer to tilt their own head back.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Type III flotation aid reliably turns an unconscious swimmer face-up in rough open water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Type IV cushions and rings are supplemental throwable aids and never replace the wearable life jacket required for each passenger.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Type IV throwable ring buoy can substitute for a wearable life jacket on short lake trips.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Coast Guard regulations prohibit anyone under sixteen years of age from using inflatable personal flotation devices on the water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Youth under sixteen may wear Coast Guard approved inflatable vests whenever they pass the swimmer test.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must lift the shoulder straps to confirm the vest does not ride up above the chin or ears before entering the water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buckling all waist straps tightly is enough to verify a proper personal flotation device fit.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a life jacket fits snugly enough during a dockside shoulder-lift test?
Under what condition does an inflatable life jacket fail to meet legal requirements for a youth operator?
Which physical indicator shows that a kapok or foam personal flotation device must be retired from service?
Where should a Scout position a Type IV throwable device on board to guarantee immediate deployment?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Portable tanks must be removed from the boat and filled on the dock with the nozzle grounded to prevent static sparks and bilge fumes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Portable fuel tanks should be filled inside the cockpit so spilled drops stay off the dock.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water trapped inside the gearcase freezes and expands during winter, cracking the aluminum lower unit housing if left unserviced.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Draining the lower unit gear oil is unnecessary before winter storage if no water leaks appear.

extra_misconceptions.fact: True inboards use a fixed shaft and rudder, causing prop walk and limited steering control when backing up at low speeds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inboard ski boats turn rapidly in reverse because the propeller pivots with the steering wheel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Marine electrical parts use flame arrestors and sealed housings so internal sparks cannot ignite gasoline vapors in the engine bay.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Automotive alternators and starters are safe drop-in replacements for marine stern-drive engines.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to untreated gasoline left inside a carburetor or fuel rail over a six-month winter layup?
Why is it dangerous to fill a portable marine fuel tank while it sits inside the boat hull?
Which physical indicator confirms that an outboard cooling water pump is circulating water after startup?
Where should a Scout position heavy spare anchors and toolboxes to preserve proper hull trim and balance?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Red even-numbered nun buoys stay on the starboard side only when returning from open sea or traveling upstream into a harbor.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Red Right Returning means a boater keeps red nun buoys on the starboard side when heading out to sea.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Power-driven vessels must generally give way to vessels under sail and human-powered craft unless overtaken or in a narrow channel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Faster motorboats always have the right-of-way over slower sailboats and rowboats in open channels.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A float plan is left with a reliable contact person ashore who can alert authorities if the group does not return by the cutoff time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filing a float plan requires registering your route with the local Coast Guard station before launch.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An orange diamond containing a cross indicates an exclusion area where all motorboats and watercraft are strictly prohibited.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: White buoys marked with an orange diamond and cross permit slow no-wake motorboating inside the zone.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to lateral buoy assignments when a motorboat transitions from heading upstream to returning seaward?
Under what condition does a power-driven vessel become the stand-on boat during a crossing encounter?
Which physical indicator on the water warns a boat crew to head for shore before thunder is audible?
What measurement confirms that an anchor line provides adequate scope for holding in rough weather?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Boats should approach a dock slowly at a shallow ten-to-twenty degree angle when wind and current are calm, then shift into reverse.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Approaching a dock at a steep ninety-degree angle gives the helm operator the best stopping control.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Throwing coiled line all at once fouls the anchor; lower it hand-over-hand from the bow and pay out five-to-seven times the depth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heaving the anchor and all of its coiled rode overboard at once sets the flukes deeper into the mud.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The cutoff lanyard must be clipped securely to the operator's wrist or life jacket so the motor stops immediately if they are thrown.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Attaching the engine cutoff switch lanyard to the steering wheel keeps it handy for the helm operator.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Boarders must keep three points of contact and step into the center of the boat first, then have someone hand equipment aboard from the dock.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passengers should carry heavy coolers and fuel cans in both hands as they step onto the boat gunwale.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position their center of gravity when stepping from a low dock into a small runabout?
What happens to boat steering control if the operator cuts the throttle completely while approaching a dock?
Why is it dangerous to clip the engine cutoff switch lanyard to a loose jacket pocket instead of your wrist or vest?
Which physical indicator on the anchor rode shows that the flukes have set firmly into the bottom sediment?
